source: make a 1+ speed obby with 10 levels and every level get more harder the further you go and there are treadmills you can run on to get more speed

image_prompt.text: A chain of platforms spaced to the physics limits, running the ordered route through all ten levels
Flat enclosed pads at each level boundary where players stop safely and respawn on failure
Long horizontal jumps, trampoline boosts and stepped vertical platforms, getting tighter each level
Treadmill conveyors the player runs along to build extra speed, plus rotating and sliding platforms
Ten sequential level segments, each visibly harder than the one before

layout_placement.text: Respawn point at the start of each of the ten levels

notes: Ten levels is a structural count with no field to carry it; recorded here so the P6 generator segments the course into ten.
Difficulty must increase monotonically along the course - an ordering constraint on obstacle selection, not a placeable feature.
The treadmill speed gain reads as a persistent stat ('1+ speed'), which the layout can only express as a conveyor surface.

open_questions.ask: No theme was stated - should the ten levels share one look, or change theme as they get harder?
Should the ten levels run along the ground or stack into a tower?

coverage_missing.ask: No theme was stated - should the ten levels share one look, or change theme as they get harder?
Should the ten levels run along the ground or stack into a tower?
Is there a reward at the end of level ten, or does it just stop?

answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the ten levels share one look, or change theme as they get harder?
answers.answer: Use one consistent simple cartoon obby look across all ten levels so the build stays clear and focused on the increasing difficulty.

answers.ask: Should the ten levels run along the ground or stack into a tower?
answers.answer: Stack the ten levels into a tower, with each higher level being harder than the last.
